changes.pattern: The decomposer over-reasons without effectively using search, causing token cuts and premature unanswerable conclusions.
changes.rationale: In A2 and A5 the decomposer wrote long exhaustive reasoning, did not run search to locate the missing fact, and either hit the token limit or concluded the answer was absent. This is a general self-harness failure of the decomposer's working method, so its role should force early tool use, concise hop-by-hop reasoning, and a search-before-unanswerable check.

ops.name: decomposer
ops.role: Split the question into single-hop sub-questions. Use search when available to find each fact and cite the paragraph. One short line per hop; do not list all paragraphs. Search for a missing fact before answering unanswerable. Give the shortest answer matching the question.

changes.pattern: The checker changes or keeps final answers that do not match the requested value: it shortens identifying person names, accepts unverified unanswerable answers, or keeps hyphenated compounds for singular country/nationality questions.
changes.rationale: In A3 the checker changed a correct full name to a shorter ambiguous name. In A2 and A5 it accepted unanswerable without searching for the missing fact. In A1 and A6 it kept a hyphenated dual-nationality phrase when the question asked for one country/nationality. These are final-answer verification and formatting failures of the checker role, so the checker role should verify with search, preserve the input unless disproven, preserve full identifying names, and match the requested singular value for country/nationality questions.

ops.name: checker
ops.role: Use search when available to verify each hop; if the input says unanswerable, search first. Keep the input answer unless proven wrong. Preserve full identifying person names. For singular country/nationality answers from a hyphenated dual nationality, use the first part for origin questions and the second part for nationality questions.

changes.pattern: Checker strips the disambiguating title from a person's full name, breaking exact match on 'who' questions
changes.rationale: In A3 the decomposer correctly produced 'John II, Prince of Anhalt-Zerbst' but the checker, following the 'shortest span' instruction in answer_span, reduced it to 'John II'. The answer_span skill needs to clarify that a person's full name including any disambiguating title is the answer span, not just the numeral or first name. This is a library-layer fix because the skill is given to both nodes and the instruction applies to every question that uses the skill.

ops.name: answer_span
ops.text: Give the shortest span that answers the question, as it appears in the paragraphs: a name, a title, a date, a number or yes/no. No explanation, no 'The answer is', no extra qualifiers; keep the original spelling. For a person's name, include the full name with any disambiguating title or descriptor exactly as written in the paragraph (e.g. a numeral plus a territorial title), not just the numeral or first name.

changes.pattern: Agents declare 'unanswerable' or 'cannot be determined' when the answer requires a one-step inference from context already present in the entity's paragraph, and the decomposer burns its token budget looping on verification
changes.rationale: In A2 the decomposer re-read the husband's paragraph repeatedly looking for an explicit 'died in X' sentence, got cut at the token limit, and the checker confirmed 'cannot be determined' even though the paragraph established the location context. In A5 the decomposer similarly looped and the checker said 'Unanswerable' even though the only location in the director's paragraph was the correct answer. The root cause is that the model treats 'not explicitly stated' as 'not in the text' and gives up instead of inferring from the closest available fact. A meta-harness rule (residual layer) tells every agent on every question that the paragraphs contain enough information and that inference from the entity's own paragraph is the correct strategy, which prevents the verification loop and the 'unanswerable' conclusion.

ops.text: Every question is answerable from the given paragraphs. If the exact phrase for a fact is not present, infer it from the closest available context in the relevant entity's paragraph (a location, date, or attribute already mentioned for that entity). Never answer 'unanswerable', 'cannot be determined', or 'not mentioned'.

changes.pattern: Decomposer enters a re-verification loop after completing the bridge chain and is cut at the token limit before producing a final answer
changes.rationale: In A5 the decomposer correctly identified the director and read the director's paragraph, then spent the remaining token budget re-scanning every paragraph and questioning whether the answer was present, ultimately getting cut off. The bridge skill's four steps end at 'read the asked property there' but give no instruction to stop, so the model adds its own verification. Adding an explicit commit step to the bridge skill (library layer, applies to every bridge question) tells the model to stop after step 3 and output the answer, preventing the loop.

ops.name: bridge
ops.when: an entity is described through another ('the director of film X', 'the city where Y was born')
ops.text: 1. Find the inner entity first (the film X), from its paragraph. 2. Read the property you need (its director) and name the bridge entity exactly. 3. Find the bridge entity's own paragraph and read the asked property there. 4. The answer is about the last entity in the chain, not the first. 5. After step 3, commit to your answer immediately. Do not re-read other paragraphs or re-verify.

changes.pattern: Decomposers ramble, hit the token limit, and conclude a fact is missing without exhaustively searching for the needed property.
changes.rationale: In A2 and A5 the decomposer produced long, cut-off reasoning and did not effectively use the search tool to locate the death-place sentence before saying the answer was unavailable. A concise, tool-first role plus a property-lookup skill targets this step directly.

ops.name: decomposer
ops.role: Answer multi-hop questions using only the given paragraphs. If tools are given, run search for the key entity and the needed property word before answering; read all matching sentences. Keep reasoning under 120 words and do not list every paragraph. Cite only the sentences you use. Say unanswerable only after searching and finding no supporting sentence. End with #### <short answer>.

ops.name: fact_lookup
ops.when: the question asks for one specific property of an entity, such as place of death, place of birth, date, location, or nationality
ops.text: 1. Identify the exact entity. 2. Run search for the entity name and for the property word plus synonyms (died/death, born/birth, place, location, date, country, nationality). 3. Read every matching sentence; do not stop at the first match. 4. Copy the exact span that states the property. 5. Answer unanswerable only if no sentence states the property.

changes.pattern: Checkers shorten a supported person answer by dropping a needed title or disambiguator.
changes.rationale: In A3 the decomposer correctly answered the full named entity, but the checker changed it to a shorter name and lost the supporting qualifier. The checker role and answer_span skill must preserve full identifying spans when the input answer is already supported.

ops.name: checker
ops.role: Check the given answer against the paragraphs. If tools are given, verify the cited sentences with search. Keep reasoning under 100 words. If the input answer is supported, preserve it, including full person names and titles; do not shorten a supported span. Change it only if a paragraph contradicts it or gives a better-supported span. End with #### <short answer>.

ops.name: answer_span
ops.text: Give the shortest span that answers the question, as it appears in the paragraphs: a name, a title, a date, a number, or yes/no. For a person, include the full name and any title or disambiguator used in the supporting paragraph when needed to distinguish similar names. No explanation, no 'The answer is', no extra qualifiers; keep the original spelling.

changes.pattern: Singular country/nationality questions are answered with a hyphenated compound nationality instead of one country component.
changes.rationale: A1 and A6 both have supporting text with a compound nationality, but the questions ask for one country/nationality and the expected answer is a single country. A residual skill for this question class can tell the model to select one component rather than returning the compound.

ops.name: nationality_country
ops.when: the question asks a person's nationality or which country they are from, especially when the paragraph may give a hyphenated nationality
ops.text: 1. Identify the person and read all sentences about them. 2. If a sentence states a single country or nationality, use that span. 3. If the only statement is a hyphenated nationality and the question asks for one country, answer one country component, not the hyphenated compound. 4. For 'which country ... from' questions, prefer the first component unless another sentence states a single country. 5. For 'what nationality' questions, prefer the component that is independently stated as a single country elsewhere; if none, prefer the component that is not the country of the work named in the question; if still unclear, use the last component.

changes.pattern: The meta-harness uses a vague skill rule and always adds a checker, so useful skills are omitted and the checker can overcorrect.
changes.rationale: The wrong teams often lacked the specific skill for the property or nationality being asked, while the checker was present even when it added risk. Making staffing and skill assignment explicit, and limiting checkers to genuinely ambiguous cases, addresses the residual harness failures without adding a new architecture.

ops.text: An entity described through another: use one decomposer with search and the matching skills. Add a checker with search only when similar names, same-title paragraphs, dates, or comparisons make verification necessary.

Give search to every node that must locate facts and answer_span to every node. Give the matching skill: bridge, relations, comparison, dates_numbers, nationality_country, or fact_lookup. Give distractors only when similar names or same-title paragraphs are present.
